summary: This note covers the 1968 single "Daddy Sang Bass," written by Carl Perkins and recorded by Johnny Cash, which incorporates lines from the chorus of "Will the Circle Be Unbroken?" It was Cash's sixty-first release on the country chart and reached No. 1 on the Billboard country chart for six weeks. The note also covers its pop chart performance, its later release in the Columbia Records Hall of Fame Series, and a 1969 CMA nomination.
one_line: A 1968 Johnny Cash single written by Carl Perkins that hit No. 1 on the Billboard country chart.
key_facts: "Daddy Sang Bass" is a 1968 single written by Carl Perkins.
The song includes lines from the chorus of "Will the Circle Be Unbroken?"
The single was recorded by Johnny Cash.
"Daddy Sang Bass" was Johnny Cash's sixty-first release on the country chart.
The song went to No. 1 on the Billboard country chart for 6 weeks.
The song spent a total of 19 weeks on the Billboard country chart.
The single reached No. 56 on the Cashbox pop singles chart in 1969.
"Daddy Sang Bass" was released on the Columbia Records Hall of Fame Series as a 45, #13-33153.
The Columbia Records Hall of Fame Series 45 was backed with a live version of "Folsom Prison Blues."
The record was nominated for Single of the Year by the Country Music Association (CMA) in 1969.
